title: Go SDK: streaming graceful reconnect and context-deadline propagation for generator streams
creator: Marco Chen
description: Users of the Go SDK have reported surprising behavior when long-running generator streams hit transient network failures or context deadlines. Current streaming primitives surface token-level cancellation via context.Context but do not coordinate reconnect/backoff semantics, nor do they propagate the original request deadline consistently across stream reconnects. This ticket designs and implements a streaming layer that: (1) preserves the original context deadline across reconnect attempts where applicable, (2) introduces a configurable graceful reconnect/backoff strategy for transient errors, (3) surfaces partial responses and final state deterministically to callers, and (4) adds telemetry and unit/integration tests to validate behavior across edge cases.
acceptance_criteria: The Go SDK streaming API propagates the caller's context deadline to any underlying retry/reconnect attempts; if the deadline expires, stream returns a context.DeadlineExceeded error and no additional reconnects are attempted.
Transient network errors (HTTP 5xx, stream reset) trigger a configurable reconnect policy with jittered exponential backoff; default policy is 3 retries with initial backoff 200ms and max backoff 2s.

Partial events already delivered to the caller prior to a disconnect remain visible and the stream resumes producing new events if reconnect succeeds; consumer-facing iterator yields an explicit 'resumed' event type in the protocol.
SDK exposes ergonomic helpers: StreamWithContext(ctx, opts) and Stream.Cancel() which respect deadlines and return consistent error values.
New unit tests cover: deadline expiration during backoff, successful reconnect within deadline, reconnect exhaustion, and correct telemetry emission for reconnect attempts.
E2E integration test runs against a flaky mock server in CI demonstrating behavior matrix; documentation in CHANGELOG and SDK streaming README updated.
Performance regression <3% for nominal streaming scenarios without errors.
Design and implementation have code review approval and an associated PR merged into release branch sdk-go-0.12.0.
design_notes: We will treat stream reconnects as orthogonal to application-level request retries: reconnect attempts only re-open the transport and resume KV cache/token position to avoid duplicate generation when the server supports continuation tokens.
Propagate context deadline by deriving a per-reconnect sub-context that has remaining time from the parent ctx, computed as deadline.Sub(time.Now()). If remaining time <= 0, abort immediately.

Add a lightweight 'stream session token' concept: server may return a continuation token; SDK will send it on reconnect to resume. If server does not support continuation, reconnect falls back to no-resume and SDK will surface a non-retriable error.
Backoff policy implemented in internal/backoff.go with options for retries, base, max, and jitter. Defaults chosen per acceptance criteria but overridable via StreamOptions.
We will not change public blocking generator semantics; provide a StreamOptions flag ResumeOnReconnect=true to opt into resume behavior because some customers rely on strict at-most-once semantics.
Telemetry: emit metrics 'sdk.stream.reconnect.attempt', 'sdk.stream.reconnect.success', and tag with model, region, error_class.
Observability: add logs at Debug for each reconnect attempt and Info for reconnect exhausted. Add trace spans around reconnect logic.
Compatibility: keep existing Stream API surface but add StreamWithContext(ctx, opts) wrapper as preferred ergonomic entrypoint. Maintain older constructors with deprecation note.
Edge cases: if reconnect succeeds but server returns duplicate tokens, SDK will detect via idempotency token header and translate to a 'duplicate_data' event that consumers can handle explicitly.
Security: no new secrets persisted. Continuation token treated as bearer token for session only and not logged in plaintext.
implementation_plan: Add types: StreamOptions struct with ResumeOnReconnect, BackoffPolicy fields. Add internal stream session token handling.
Implement backoff helper with jitter and unit tests.
Wire up context deadline propagation logic in stream connect path; add unit tests for remaining time calculation and immediate-abort paths.
Extend transport layer to accept continuation token header 'X-Stream-Continuation' and include parsing logic for server responses.
Implement high-level StreamWithContext API and update existing examples to use it.
Add telemetry hooks and trace spans in reconnect path; add CI integration test using flaky server harness.
Write comprehensive unit tests and integration test scenarios in sdk-go/integration/flaky-server. Add an OSS example under examples/streaming-reconnect.
Open PR, iterate on review feedback, land under feature flag for one cycle if needed, then enable by default in sdk-go-0.12.0.
Update SDK README streaming section and add migration notes for consumers.
Monitor rollout using metrics dashboard and error-rate alert thresholds.
Post-merge: schedule follow-up to instrument real-customer usage and tune defaults.
Estimated dev: 3 dev days + 1 day for tests + 1 day for docs/release prep.
Risk: server-side continuation token semantics vary; mitigation: opt-in resume flag and safe fallback to fail-fast with clear error message.
testing_steps: Unit tests: backoff jitter distribution, remaining-deadline calculation, immediate-deadline-abort.
Mock server tests: simulate connection reset after N bytes, verify SDK reconnects and resumes with continuation token; verify correct error when server doesn't support resume.
Integration flaky harness: run E2E with network delay and packet drops to reproduce transient resets; validate metrics emitted.
Manual QA: sample app in examples/streaming-reconnect, exercise Cancel() from a goroutine and confirm stream terminates promptly and resources are cleaned up.
Load test: baseline streaming throughput with and without reconnect instrumentation to confirm <3% regression.
CI: add flaky-server matrix to pipeline that runs integration test once per PR.
Security review: confirm continuation tokens are not logged and trace sampling respects PII rules.
Documentation: confirm README snippet and CHANGELOG entry added and validated by docs reviewer.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: resuming streams can lead to duplicates if server semantics not idempotent. Mitigation: default ResumeOnReconnect=false and explicit opt-in; preserve at-most-once semantics by default.

Risk: developers expect context cancellation to always abort immediately; edge cases may show delayed abort during in-flight reconnect backoff. Mitigation: compute remaining time and fail-fast if insufficient time for next attempt; document behavior clearly.
Risk: increasing surface area of streaming API may confuse users. Mitigation: provide ergonomic helpers and examples, keep original API functional with deprecation schedule.
Risk: misconfigured backoff can cause thundering reconnect storms. Mitigation: provide sane defaults and server-side rate limiting compatibility notes.
Risk: telemetry noise during rollout. Mitigation: tag reconnect metrics with feature_flag and add sampling control.
